epics.summary: Decision routing to the plan owner (ADR 0006)

stories.summary: Let a plan's owner and delegates answer its decisions
stories.description: ADR 0006 item 3 and ADR 0009's delegate role: the owner and delegates may answer a plan's decisions. LocalPolicy grants ownership only approve/reject/merge today.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83, STACKED on the enterprise-enforcement-closeout stand-in (this plan is blocked_by ENF-03) - a stand-in of every story in decision-routing and system-principals applied together with it. First run 3 conflicts in this plan: tests/unit/test_notification_routing.py::test_validation_failures_raise[<lambda>-not supported yet0] (pins `match.owner` as unsupported - pre-authorized in RT-03), tests/unit/test_oa2_request_decision_failopen.py::test_success_path_return_and_record_unchanged (exact record equality - pre-authorized in RT-02); the third was the unknown-key case, fixed by keeping the 'not supported yet' wording. Re-run with the resolutions: 17746 passed / 21 skipped; the only remaining failure is ENF-02's pre-authorized test_save_plan_unchanged (its edit was not applied in the stand-in). Four other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is the root user's home, which the guard bans by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary).

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: `app/policy.py` `LocalPolicy.allow` grants a plan's owner and delegates exactly `plan:approve`, `plan:reject` and `story:merge`. ADR 0006 (Accepted) says decisions escalate to the owner and delegates may answer; ADR 0009 section 3 defines `delegate` as "may answer decisions". Today only the local operator can answer one (`app/dashboard.py` asks `authorize("decision:answer", ...)`).

WHAT TO BUILD: add `Action.DECISION_ANSWER` to the tuple of actions ownership grants in `LocalPolicy.allow`, and update the class docstring (ownership now governs four actions; still additive only; a plan with no owner falls through to the role rule). Nothing else in the policy changes.

DOCS: docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 2 "Enforcement" (the sentence listing what owners/delegates may do) and section 6 step 2; ADR 0009's implementation-status note if it lists the owner grants.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_decision_answer_ownership.py): owner allowed `decision:answer` on their plan; delegate allowed; a third principal denied; owner of plan A denied on plan B; a plan with no owner denies a non-operator; the ownership grant still does NOT extend to `story:patch`, `plan:dispatch`, `plan:ingest` or `config:write` (one assertion each); through the dashboard route (FastAPI TestClient with a bound principal, as the existing dashboard decision tests do) an owner's answer is accepted and a stranger's gets 403/refusal with no decision written.

GENERAL RULES (every step of this story):
- Write the failing tests first (CLAUDE.md Step 3) and confirm they fail on an assertion, not an import error.
- Verify with the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; all must be green before you finish. Report pass/fail counts in the PR description.
- A new test file that imports any `pipeline.*` module must `import pipeline.server` first (pre-existing import cycle). Copy the idiom in tests/unit/test_triage_cap_silent_skip.py.
- Bind a non-operator principal in tests the way tests/unit/test_patch_plan_enforcement.py does (`pipeline.actor.bind_principal`); never add an `actor` parameter to any MCP tool (a guard test forbids it).
- The harness scratchpad `.agent_scratchpad.md` stays untracked. Commit only the files this brief names plus the new test files it asks for. Add no helper scripts, dumps or module copies.
- Never modify an existing test except as this brief pre-authorizes, with the literal edit given. If another pre-existing test fails because of a change this brief requires, do NOT undo the required change - stop and report the conflict, naming the test and the requirement it contradicts.
- Comments and docs you write must stay true after later stories merge: state the invariant, never "until story X lands".
- Cumulative artifacts (the REFERENCE.md policy table, the IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 rows, `REMOTE_*` sets): assert only what YOU add or remove (membership/absence), never the full contents, an exact count, or a hash.
- Error messages and logs name the action and the principal subject only - never a token, secret, payload, path or exception text (Secure-by-Design).
- Commit message: Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, subject <=72 chars), body explains why; put the story key in the body. If you change an existing test as pre-authorized, the body must say which test and why (CLAUDE.md Step 4).

stories.summary: Record the owner as the routing target on decisions escalated to a human
stories.description: ADR 0006 item 3: anything the overlord escalates goes to the plan owner. Stamp the target on the decision record and the escalation notice.

WHY: `pipeline/service_decisions.py` `_request_decision_impl` appends every ruling with `decided_by: "overlord"`, and on an overlord failure parks the story and notifies - but nothing says WHO must now answer. ADR 0006 routes it to the plan owner (and delegates).

WHAT TO BUILD (one file of production code plus docs):
1. A helper `_routing_target(plan_name) -> dict` in pipeline/service_decisions.py returning `{"owner": <manifest owner, or "local-operator" when the manifest has none>, "delegates": [<manifest delegates>]}`; an unreadable manifest yields the local-operator default (never raises).
2. Stamp `routed_to: _routing_target(plan_name)` and `requested_by: actor_id()` (pipeline.actor) on (a) the fail-open record and (b) any ruling whose parsed action escalates to a human. Read `_parse_ruling`'s output contract in pipeline/parsers.py first and name the exact keys/values that mean "a human must answer" in your commit body (expected: action `park_for_human` or a truthy `notify_user`). A ruling the overlord settles itself gets `requested_by` only.
3. The fail-open `_notify_user` message names the owner: "... see decisions log (routed to <owner>)". Do not add new kwargs to `_notify_user`.

DOCS: docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 6 step 2 (routing target recorded; delivery is RT-03) and REFERENCE.md's decisions-log field list if it enumerates record fields (add the two fields; membership only).

AUTHORIZED EDIT TO AN EXISTING TEST (exactly this): tests/unit/test_oa2_request_decision_failopen.py::test_success_path_return_and_record_unchanged pins the success-path record by exact equality, and its canned ruling has action `park_for_human`, so it now gains the two fields. In its expected dict, immediately after the line `        "decided_by": "overlord",` insert the two lines `        "requested_by": "local-operator",` and `        "routed_to": {"owner": "local-operator", "delegates": []},` (the seeded plan has no owner and the test binds no principal). Nothing else in that file changes. Justification for the commit body: the test guards the success path against the fail-open change; this story legitimately adds routing fields to escalated records.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_decision_routing_target.py; patch `pipeline.server._invoke_overlord`): an escalating ruling on an owned plan records `routed_to.owner == <owner>` and the delegates; an un-owned plan records `local-operator`; the fail-open path records it and its notification message contains the owner; a self-settled ruling has no `routed_to`; `requested_by` is the bound principal's subject; an unreadable manifest does not raise.

stories.summary: Deliver notifications by plan owner through an owner match on notification routes
stories.description: Per-principal notifications (ADR 0008 stage 1): a notification route can match the plan's owner, so an escalation reaches the person who must answer.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83, STACKED on the enterprise-enforcement-closeout stand-in (this plan is blocked_by ENF-03) - a stand-in of every story in decision-routing and system-principals applied together with it. TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: `pipeline/notification_routing.py` routes match only `{"plan": "<glob>"}`. On a shared server every owner's escalations would go to the same channels.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. notification_routing.py: a route's `match` object accepts an optional `owner` glob next to `plan`. Validation: `owner`, when present, must be a non-empty string (reject anything else with the existing `NotificationConfigError` style, naming the key path). Every other `match` key stays rejected, and its message must still contain "not supported yet" (tests/unit/test_notification_routing.py's `other="x"` case asserts it), e.g. "not supported yet; only 'plan' and 'owner' are allowed". `NotificationConfig.resolve(plan, event, owner="")` - a route with an `owner` glob matches only when BOTH globs match (`fnmatch.fnmatchcase`); an empty owner never matches an owner glob (deny by default). Existing routes without `owner` behave exactly as today. First-match-wins semantics are unchanged.
2. pipeline/notification_outbox.py (the spool at the `config.resolve(plan, evt_name)` call): pass the plan manifest's `owner` (read via `pipeline.store.FileStore().get_manifest`; any read error -> ""). Read it once per spool call, not per instance.
3. REFERENCE.md notification-config section: document `match.owner` with one example route that sends `decision`/`overlord_failure` events for plans owned by `alice@example.com` to her channel instance.

AUTHORIZED EDIT TO AN EXISTING TEST (exactly this): in tests/unit/test_notification_routing.py's `test_validation_failures_raise` parameter list, delete the single entry `    (lambda c: c["routes"][0]["match"].update(owner="me"), "not supported yet"),`. It pins `match.owner` as unsupported, which is exactly what this story changes; your new file asserts the replacement behavior. Keep the `other="x"` entry. Justification for the commit body: requested behavior change, not a loosened check.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_notification_owner_routing.py): owner+plan route matches only that owner; plan-only route unchanged (regression); empty/unknown owner does not match an owner route; first-match-wins holds when an owner route precedes a catch-all; non-string/empty `owner` in config is rejected with the key path in the message and no secret echoed; the outbox spools an owned plan's event to the owner's instance and an unreadable manifest falls through to plan-only routes.
